clue.text: Covers up church backing scam and losing nothing

indicators.note: the church comes after, as if backing up, the scam

parts.note: a con is a swindle or scam
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: losing means the next item is taken out of the word for 'and'

parts.note: 'also' is a synonym of 'and'
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A church hushes up a fraud and the money lost in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes O out of ALSO to leave ALS.
explanation.definitionFit: To conceal things is to hide them, which is what covering up means.

clue.text: Adviser thought to have advanced to highest level

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the start, so this letter is promoted to the front of the word for thought

parts.note: an idea is a thought

explanation.surface: An adviser's thinking has earned promotion to the top tier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advanced to highest level' moves the A of IDEA to the top, giving AIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is an assistant or adviser to someone senior.

clue.text: Cost of hiring detective is criminal

parts.note: PI is a private investigator, a detective
a rate is a charge for hiring someone by the hour or day

explanation.surface: The fee a private eye charges is daylight robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cost of hiring detective' reads as one charge, but the two parts are separate and set in the answer's order.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate is a robber at sea, so a criminal.

clue.text: Last section of work records interrupted by one void update

indicators.note: interrupted means something breaks into the records

parts.note: two kinds of record: an EP (extended-play disc) and a log
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: void means emptied, so only the outside letters of update remain

explanation.surface: The closing part of a book holds records spoiled by an empty revision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'records' gives two record types, side by side, which 'interrupted by' splits with the one.
explanation.definitionFit: An epilogue is the closing passage of a book or play.

clue.text: Revoking terms of public user signed in by mistake

indicators.note: letters arranged by mistake are jumbled
terms are ends, so the last letters of the two words are taken

explanation.surface: Cancelling a public user's account because they were logged in in error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terms of' gives C and R; 'by mistake' shuffles them with SIGNED IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescind a law or order is to revoke or cancel it.

clue.text: Joyful expression encapsulating the author's particular way with words

indicators.note: encapsulating means holding inside, so the author goes within

parts.note: a smile is a joyful facial expression
the author refers to himself as I; 'the author's' reads as 'the author is'

explanation.surface: A happy look hints at a writer's distinctive turn of phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encapsulating' puts I inside SMILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A simile is a figure of speech comparing one thing to another: a particular use of language.

clue.text: Monitors adopting international codes of practice?

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the international abbreviation goes inside

parts.note: polices means oversees or monitors

explanation.surface: Watchdogs take on worldwide standards of conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopting' puts I into POLICES.
explanation.definitionFit: Policies are rules or principles of conduct, which the question mark admits are like codes of practice.

clue.text: Push student to use clearing process?

parts.note: to shove is to push
L for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: Pressure a student into going through a clearing scheme for places.
explanation.walkthrough: Clearing in the UK is the scheme that matches leftover university places to students, so the surface is about admissions; the definition means clearing snow or earth.
explanation.definitionFit: To shovel is to clear snow or earth with a spade-like tool, a clearing process.

clue.text: Represent content of new script briefly?

definitions.text: Represent content of new script briefly?

indicators.note: to re-present letters is to set them out again in a new order
the content is the inside, the middle letter of the word
briefly means cut short, losing the last letter

explanation.surface: Summarise what a fresh script says in a few words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content of' gives E from new; 'briefly' trims script to SCRIP; 'Represent' shuffles E and SCRIP. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A precis is a summary, so to precis is to restate content briefly.

clue.text: Unit equal to inverse of time divided by speed of light

indicators.note: divided by means split, with the light-speed symbol in the middle
inverse means turned the other way round, so the word for time runs backwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time
c is the physics symbol for the speed of light

explanation.surface: A physics formula: a unit equal to reciprocal time over c.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inverse of' turns ERA into ARE; 'divided by' splits it with C. The maths language is all misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, 4,840 square yards.

clue.text: Furious tech company admitting nothing initially causes tension in court

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so nothing goes inside the company name

parts.note: Apple is the computer and phone company
O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of the next four words are taken

explanation.surface: An angry technology giant denies wrongdoing as a legal battle gets tense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admitting' puts O into APPLE; 'initially' takes CTIC from causes tension in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Apoplectic means so angry one seems close to a fit.

clue.text: Prime minister cut short by Queen is upset

indicators.note: by means beside, so the queen and the shortened prime minister sit side by side

parts.note: R is for Regina, Latin for queen

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is removed

parts.note: Clement Attlee was the UK prime minister from 1945 to 1951

explanation.surface: A prime minister is curtailed by the monarch and is distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' removes the final E of ATTLEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle someone is to unsettle or upset them.

clue.text: Instrument in boat beginning to monitor polluted water

indicators.note: polluted means fouled, so these letters are jumbled
the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to pass water is to urinate, so urine is water

explanation.surface: A device inside a boat starts to check dirty water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polluted' looks like it describes water, but it scrambles BOAT and M (from 'beginning to monitor') into TAMBO.
explanation.definitionFit: A tambourine is a percussion instrument, a small drum with jingles.

clue.text: Stop being inspired by fresh green produce

indicators.note: inspired means breathed in, so the stop goes inside
fresh means new, so the letters are arranged anew

parts.note: to end is to stop

explanation.surface: Stop being motivated by new green produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' makes ENGER from green; 'being inspired by' puts END inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To engender is to bring about or produce a feeling or situation.

clue.text: Bridge is blocked by American boat

indicators.note: blocked means something stands inside, so the American abbreviation goes within

parts.note: a span is a bridge or the arch of one

explanation.surface: An American vessel is in the way of a bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A sampan is a flat-bottomed boat used in East Asia.

clue.text: Debut of Michael Caine as criminal is one to forget

indicators.note: criminal means bad or wrong, so the letters are jumbled
a debut is a first appearance, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Michael Caine's first film role as a crook is forgettable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' shuffles M, CAINE and AS.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesiac is a person suffering memory loss: someone who forgets.

clue.text: Give up on board divulging information?

parts.note: re means on, concerning
a sign is a board displaying information

explanation.surface: A board member quits after spilling secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' looks like membership of a board, but 'on' and 'board' work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to give up a job or post.

clue.text: Backward child going round bend lives in drug-induced state

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the child wraps the bend
backward means written the wrong way round

parts.note: a son is a child
an arc is a curve or bend
is means exists, lives

explanation.surface: A slow child taking a corner lives in a drugged haze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' reverses the child, which 'going round' then wraps around the bend.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcosis is stupor or unconsciousness caused by narcotics.

clue.text: Broadcast part of breakfast TV programme in instalments

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the airwaves, so the sound of the word counts

parts.note: cereal is eaten at breakfast

explanation.surface: A slot from a morning TV show is aired in episodes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' signals that CEREAL is heard, giving SERIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A serial is a story shown in episodes over several broadcasts.

clue.text: Sponge divers source shell from galleon

indicators.note: divers is an old word for various, so the letters are in a different order
a shell is the outside, so the first and last letters are taken

explanation.surface: Undersea divers get sponges and shells from a sunken galleon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' (meaning various) shuffles SOURCE with GN (the 'shell from galleon').
explanation.definitionFit: To sponge is to live off others, which is to scrounge.

clue.text: Lead singer may perform series of concerts on radio

parts.note: can means is able or may perform

indicators.note: on radio means heard rather than seen, so the sound of the word counts

parts.note: a tour is a run of concerts

explanation.surface: The band's frontman might play a set of gigs on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on radio' turns TOUR into TOR by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantor leads the singing in a synagogue or church choir.

clue.text: This material, close to chintz, can be made into organza

indicators.note: made into means reworked, so the letters are rearranged into the fabric
the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A fabric that, near chintz, can be woven into organza.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be made into' says this word's letters plus Z (from 'close to chintz') rearrange into ORGANZA.
explanation.definitionFit: Angora is a soft fabric made from goat or rabbit hair.

clue.text: Car repairers replacing casing of engine causes complaint

indicators.note: replacing means the repairers take the place of the outer letters, so they wrap what is left

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a UK breakdown service

indicators.note: the casing is the outside, which is stripped to leave the middle letters

explanation.surface: Mechanics swapping an engine's housing causes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing casing of' strips the outer Es of ENGINE and puts AA there instead; the AA is the Automobile Association, a UK breakdown service.
explanation.definitionFit: Angina is a heart condition, a medical complaint.

clue.text: Total profit in English banks providing high interest rate

indicators.note: banks means sits either side, so English surrounds the profit

parts.note: gross is total earnings before deductions

explanation.surface: A total profit in English banks gives a high interest rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' is the containment signal, not financial institutions; the money picture makes 'interest' look monetary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something engrossing absorbs the attention, so it is of great interest.

clue.text: Small advance by one member in workplace

parts.note: S is for small
a hop is a jump forward on one leg

explanation.surface: A minor step forward for one employee at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop is a workshop, a place where things are made or repaired.

clue.text: Short month's end appears earlier than usual in part of March?

indicators.note: the final letter turns up sooner than it normally would

parts.note: Sept is short for September

explanation.surface: A month's close coming early in the March calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: The final T of SEPT moves forward to give STEP. March here is marching, not the month.
explanation.definitionFit: A march is made up of steps, so a step is part of it.

clue.text: Reporter's relatively hackneyed cover for The Observer

indicators.note: a reporter speaks, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: cornier means more trite, more hackneyed

explanation.surface: A journalist's comparatively clichéd piece for The Observer newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, but here it is anyone who observes, whose eye the cornea covers.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornea is the transparent front layer covering the eye, which an observer uses.

clue.text: Girlie magazine's ultimate shot captures woman's rear in this

definitions.text: Girlie magazine's ultimate shot captures woman's rear in this

indicators.note: captures means holds within
shot means ruined, so the letters are jumbled
the rear of a word is its last letter
ultimate means last, so the final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A men's magazine's final photo shows a woman's behind in underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' jumbles GIRLIE into LIGERI and 'captures' puts N inside it. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is women's underwear, the sort such a photo might feature.
